1 Purpose

This RMarkdown file documents a replication of Nagano (2015), “Demographics of Adult Heritage Language Speakers in the United States: Differences by Region and Language and Their Implications,” using the reduced IPUMS extracts in data/.

The goal is a faithful reconstruction of the paper’s descriptive analyses:

  • Race/ethnicity and Hispanic-origin summaries for 1980, 1990, 2000, and 2010.
  • Broad estimates of people who speak a language other than English at home.
  • Narrow estimates of adult heritage language (HL) speakers.
  • State-level counts and proportions of adult HL speakers.
  • Language-level counts, shares, and growth rates.
  • State-specific language profiles for California, Texas, New York, Florida, and New Mexico.
  • Gini indexes for the geographic concentration of adult HL speakers by language.

The data files are reduced samples of the original research data, so exact numerical matches to the published article are not expected. The central ordering of states/languages and the substantive patterns should be close.

2 Paper-Based Analytic Definition

Nagano (2015) defines adult HL speakers operationally using the variables available in the U.S. Census/ACS via IPUMS. The target respondents are people who:

  1. are age 18 or older;
  2. speak a language other than English at home;
  3. report at least some English speaking ability, excluding those who “do not speak English”; and
  4. if foreign-born, immigrated to the United States at age 18 or younger.

In this notebook, this definition is translated as follows:

  • AGE >= 18
  • LANGUAGE is not missing/blank and is not English: !LANGUAGE %in% c(0, 1)
  • SPEAKENG is not missing and is not “Does not speak English”: SPEAKENG %in% c(2, 4, 5, 6)
  • U.S.-born respondents are those with BPL <= 120, which includes the 50 states, D.C., unspecified U.S., Native American, Puerto Rico, and other U.S. possessions in the IPUMS coding scheme.
  • Foreign-born respondents are retained when their approximate age at immigration is 18 or younger: YEAR - YRIMMIG <= 18.

The last item is approximate because the public-use files provide year of immigration rather than exact age at arrival.

3 Load Packages and Data

library(dplyr)
library(forcats)
library(ggplot2)
library(haven)
library(knitr)
library(readr)
library(scales)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
data_dir <- "data"
data_files <- list.files(data_dir, pattern = "[.]sav$", full.names = TRUE)
data_files <- data_files[order(readr::parse_number(basename(data_files)))]
basename(data_files)
## [1] "DATA_DOWNLOADED_FROM_IPUMS_SAMPLE1980.sav"
## [2] "DATA_DOWNLOADED_FROM_IPUMS_SAMPLE1990.sav"
## [3] "DATA_DOWNLOADED_FROM_IPUMS_SAMPLE2000.sav"

Only the variables needed for this replication are loaded. This keeps the analysis closer to the published methods while reducing memory use.

vars_needed <- c(
  "YEAR", "STATEFIP", "CONSPUMA", "PERWT", "AGE", "BPL", "YRIMMIG",
  "LANGUAGE", "SPEAKENG", "RACESING", "HISPAN"
)

read_ipums_file <- function(path) {
  message("Reading ", basename(path))
  haven::read_sav(path, col_select = any_of(vars_needed)) |>
    mutate(source_file = basename(path))
}

raw <- data_files |>
  lapply(read_ipums_file) |>
  bind_rows()

4 Labels and Helper Functions

label_lookup <- function(x) {
  labs <- attr(x, "labels")
  tibble(
    value = as.numeric(labs),
    label = names(labs)
  )
}

state_lookup <- label_lookup(raw$STATEFIP) |>
  rename(state_code = value, state = label)

race_lookup <- label_lookup(raw$RACESING) |>
  rename(race_code = value, race = label)

hispan_lookup <- label_lookup(raw$HISPAN) |>
  rename(hispan_code = value, hispanic_origin = label)

language_lookup <- label_lookup(raw$LANGUAGE) |>
  rename(language_code = value, language = label) |>
  mutate(
    language = str_replace_all(language, "/", " "),
    language = str_replace_all(language, "East Southeast", "East/Southeast")
  )

pct_change <- function(new, old) {
  ifelse(is.na(old) | old == 0, NA_real_, (new - old) / old)
}

average_decade_increase <- function(x, years = c(1980, 1990, 2000, 2010)) {
  x <- x[match(years, names(x))]
  mean(c(
    pct_change(x[2], x[1]),
    pct_change(x[3], x[2]),
    pct_change(x[4], x[3])
  ), na.rm = TRUE)
}

average_decade_from_columns <- function(df) {
  decade_cols <- c("1980", "1990", "2000", "2010")
  apply(as.data.frame(df[decade_cols]), 1, average_decade_increase)
}

weighted_n <- function(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)

fmt_n <- function(x) comma(round(x, 0), accuracy = 1)
fmt_pct <- function(x) percent(x, accuracy = 0.01)

gini <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0 || sum(x) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  x <- sort(x)
  n <- length(x)
  (2 * sum(seq_along(x) * x) / (n * sum(x))) - ((n + 1) / n)
}
analytic <- raw |>
  mutate(
    state_code = as.numeric(STATEFIP),
    language_code = as.numeric(LANGUAGE),
    race_code = as.numeric(RACESING),
    hispan_code = as.numeric(HISPAN),
    perwt = as.numeric(PERWT),
    age = as.numeric(AGE),
    bpl = as.numeric(BPL),
    yrimmig = as.numeric(YRIMMIG),
    speakeng = as.numeric(SPEAKENG),
    year = as.numeric(YEAR),
    state_conspuma = paste(state_code, as.numeric(CONSPUMA), sep = "_"),
    us_born = bpl <= 120,
    age_at_immigration = if_else(!us_born & yrimmig > 0, year - yrimmig, NA_real_),
    speaks_lote_home = !language_code %in% c(0, 1, 95, 99),
    speaks_some_english = speakeng %in% c(2, 4, 5, 6),
    arrived_by_18_or_us_born = us_born | (!is.na(age_at_immigration) & age_at_immigration <= 18),
    adult_hl = age >= 18 & speaks_lote_home & speaks_some_english & arrived_by_18_or_us_born
  ) |>
  left_join(state_lookup, by = "state_code") |>
  left_join(language_lookup, by = "language_code") |>
  left_join(race_lookup, by = "race_code") |>
  left_join(hispan_lookup, by = "hispan_code")

analytic |>
  count(year, adult_hl)

5 Table 3: Race/Ethnicity

The paper’s Table 3 reports weighted population totals by RACESING for 1980, 1990, 2000, and 2010, plus the average decade-to-decade increase.

race_table <- analytic |>
  filter(!is.na(race)) |>
  group_by(race, year) |>
  summarise(n = weighted_n(perwt), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(`Average Increase` = average_decade_from_columns(pick(everything()))) |>
  arrange(desc(`2010`))

total_population <- analytic |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(n = weighted_n(perwt), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = n) |>
  mutate(race = "Total Population",
         `Average Increase` = average_decade_from_columns(pick(everything()))) |>
  select(race, everything())

bind_rows(total_population, race_table) |>
  mutate(across(c(`1980`, `1990`, `2000`, `2010`), fmt_n),
         `Average Increase` = fmt_pct(`Average Increase`)) |>
  kable(caption = "Replication of Table 3: Race/Ethnicity Data")

6 Table 4: Hispanic or Latino Origin

The paper’s Table 4 reports weighted population totals by HISPAN.

hispan_table <- analytic |>
  filter(!is.na(hispanic_origin), hispanic_origin != "Not Reported") |>
  group_by(hispanic_origin, year) |>
  summarise(n = weighted_n(perwt), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(`Average Increase` = average_decade_from_columns(pick(everything()))) |>
  arrange(match(hispanic_origin, c("Not Hispanic", "Mexican", "Puerto Rican", "Cuban", "Other")))

bind_rows(
  total_population |> rename(hispanic_origin = race),
  hispan_table
) |>

  kable(caption = "Replication of Table 4: Hispanic or Latino Origin Data")

7 Figures 1 and 2: State Counts in 2010

Figure 1 uses a broad home-language definition: all respondents who speak a language other than English at home. Figure 2 applies the narrower adult-HL definition used in the main analysis.

fig1_data <- analytic |>
  filter(year == 2010, speaks_lote_home) |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarise(n = weighted_n(perwt), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 10) |>
  arrange(n) |>
  mutate(label = paste0(fmt_n(n), " spks\n(", fmt_pct(prop), ")"),
         state = fct_reorder(state, n))

ggplot(fig1_data, aes(x = state, y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "gray35") +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), hjust = -0.05, size = 3.3) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +
  labs(
    title = "2010 respondents who speak languages other than English at home",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Estimated number of speakers"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

fig2_data <- analytic |>
  filter(year == 2010, adult_hl) |>
  group_by(state) |>
  summarise(n = weighted_n(perwt), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 10) |>
  arrange(n) |>
  mutate(label = paste0(fmt_n(n), " spks\n(", fmt_pct(prop), ")"),
         state = fct_reorder(state, n))

ggplot(fig2_data, aes(x = state, y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "gray35") +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), hjust = -0.05, size = 3.3) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +
  labs(
    title = "2010 adult HL speakers with at least some English proficiency",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Estimated number of speakers"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

9 Table 6: Proportion of Adult HL Speakers in Each State

state_pop <- analytic |>
  filter(!is.na(state), state != "State not identified") |>
  group_by(state, year) |>
  summarise(pop = weighted_n(perwt), .groups = "drop")

state_hl_long <- analytic |>
  filter(adult_hl, !is.na(state), state != "State not identified") |>
  group_by(state, year) |>
  summarise(hl = weighted_n(perwt), .groups = "drop")

state_prop <- state_pop |>
  left_join(state_hl_long, by = c("state", "year")) |>
  mutate(hl = replace_na(hl, 0), prop = hl / pop) |>
  select(state, year, prop) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = prop) |>
  mutate(`Difference Between 2010 and 1980` = `2010` - `1980`) |>
  arrange(state)

state_prop |>
  mutate(across(c(`1980`, `1990`, `2000`, `2010`, `Difference Between 2010 and 1980`), fmt_pct)) |>
  kable(caption = "Replication of Table 6: Adult HL Speakers as a Share of State Population")

10 Table 7: Adult HL Speakers by Language

language_counts <- analytic |>
  filter(adult_hl, !is.na(language), !language %in% c("No language", "Other or not reported", "Not reported, blank")) |>
  group_by(language, year) |>
  summarise(n = weighted_n(perwt), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    `Percentage in 2010` = `2010` / sum(`2010`, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Average Increase Rate per Decade` = average_decade_from_columns(pick(everything()))
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(`2010`))

language_total <- analytic |>
  filter(adult_hl) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(n = weighted_n(perwt), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = n) |>
  mutate(language = "ALL",
         `Percentage in 2010` = 1,
         `Average Increase Rate per Decade` = average_decade_from_columns(pick(everything()))) |>
  select(language, everything())

bind_rows(language_counts, language_total) |>
  mutate(across(c(`1980`, `1990`, `2000`, `2010`), fmt_n),
         `Percentage in 2010` = fmt_pct(`Percentage in 2010`),
         `Average Increase Rate per Decade` = fmt_pct(`Average Increase Rate per Decade`)) |>
  kable(caption = "Replication of Table 7: Adult HL Speakers by Language")

11 Figure 3: Fifteen Most Common HLs in Selected States

selected_states <- c("California", "Texas", "New York", "Florida", "New Mexico")

fig3_data <- analytic |>
  filter(year == 2010, adult_hl, state %in% selected_states, !is.na(language)) |>
  group_by(state, language) |>
  summarise(n = weighted_n(perwt), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(state) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 15, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(label = paste0(fmt_n(n), " spks (", fmt_pct(prop), ")"))

ggplot(fig3_data, aes(x = n, y = fct_reorder(language, n))) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, color = "gray20") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = n, yend = fct_reorder(language, n)), color = "gray70") +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), hjust = -0.04, size = 2.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ state, scales = "free", ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) +
  labs(
    title = "Fifteen most common adult HLs in selected states, 2010",
    x = "Estimated number of speakers",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

12 Table 8: Gini Index of Adult HL Speakers by Language

The paper uses the Gini index as a measure of geographic concentration. A value near 0 means a language group is evenly distributed across geographic units; a value near 1 means the group is concentrated in a small number of units.

For this replication, the geographic unit is the state-specific CONSPUMA, matching the paper’s note that ConsPUMA is the sample unit. Zero-speaker ConsPUMAs are included for each language-year combination so that the Gini index captures concentration rather than only dispersion among non-zero areas.

gini_years <- c(1980, 2000, 2010)

geo_units <- analytic |>
  filter(year %in% gini_years) |>
  distinct(year, state_conspuma)

language_years <- analytic |>
  filter(year %in% gini_years, adult_hl, !is.na(language)) |>
  distinct(year, language)

geo_language_counts <- analytic |>
  filter(year %in% gini_years, adult_hl, !is.na(language)) |>
  group_by(year, state_conspuma, language) |>
  summarise(n = weighted_n(perwt), .groups = "drop")

gini_table <- language_years |>
  inner_join(geo_units, by = "year") |>
  left_join(geo_language_counts, by = c("year", "state_conspuma", "language")) |>
  mutate(n = replace_na(n, 0)) |>
  group_by(language, year) |>
  summarise(gini = gini(n), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = gini) |>
  mutate(`Change 1980-2010` = `2010` - `1980`) |>
  arrange(desc(`2010`))

gini_table |>
  mutate(across(c(`1980`, `2000`, `2010`, `Change 1980-2010`), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  kable(caption = "Replication of Table 8: Gini Index by Language")

13 Replication Notes

The code above follows the published workflow as closely as the available public-use variables allow. Important implementation choices are:

  • The notebook uses PERWT for all population estimates, matching IPUMS person-level weighting conventions.
  • The broad home-language estimate excludes English, blank, no-language, and not-reported language categories.
  • The adult-HL estimate excludes respondents who report no English speaking ability.
  • Foreign-born respondents are included only if YEAR - YRIMMIG <= 18.
  • U.S. territories and U.S. possessions are treated as U.S.-born locations for the arrival-age filter because IPUMS includes them in the U.S. birthplace block.
  • The Gini calculation uses state-specific ConsPUMA identifiers, because ConsPUMA codes may repeat across states.

Likely sources of differences from the published article include:

  • These files are reduced samples rather than the full research extracts.
  • IPUMS language coding changed over time, especially for Native American language categories; some categories exist in only some years.
  • The paper’s printed figures and tables may have included additional manual recoding or formatting not documented in the article.
  • Age at immigration is approximated from year of immigration and census year.
